div.head: I Cn 20
div.ab: Uton don eac georne, swa we gyt læran wyllað: utan beon á urum hlaforde holde ⁊ getrywe ⁊ æfre eallum mihtum his wurðscipe ræran ⁊ his willan gewyrcan.
Uton don eac, swa gyt we læran wyllað: uton beon á urum hlaforde holde ⁊ getrywe ⁊ æfre eallum mihtum his wurþscipes ræran ⁊ his willan geweorcan.
Uton don eac georne, swá we gyt læran wyllað: uton beon á urum hlaforde holde ⁊ getréowe ⁊ æfre eallum mihtum his wurðscipe ræran ⁊ his willan gewyrcean.
Item faciamus, sicut adhuc persuadere uolumus: simus dominis nostris per omnia fideles et credibiles et eorum gloriam totis uiribus exaltemus et uelle faciamus,
Uton don eac georne swá we gyt læran wyllað; uton beon á urum hlaforde holde ⁊ getréowe ⁊ æfre eallum mihtum his wurðscipe ræran ⁊ his willan gewyrcean.
Let us likewise zealously carry out what we further desire to enjoin: let us ever be faithful and true to our lord, and always, with all our might, promote his honour and carry out his will.
Lasst uns auch willig handeln, wie wir nunmehr vorschreiben wollen: lasst uns stets unserem Herrn hold und getreu sein und immer mit aller Macht seinen Ehrenrang erhöhen und seinen Wunsch ausführen.
Let us also act eagerly, as we will now further instruct: let us always be loyal and faithful to our lord, and ever with all our might exalt his honour and do his will.
div.note: Liebermann compares Swer 1.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
